task_message:
Case V34: segment the vascular soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 241x241x264 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
The case is complete. 

**Summary of what I did:**

1. **Located the lesion** — A large T2-hyperintense, lobulated soft-tissue mass in the right thigh (anterior compartment), spanning roughly axial slices 83–214 (~13 cm craniocaudally), 6 cm AP and 6 cm laterally.

2. **Seeded the model** with three positive points spread across both the very bright nodular component and the intermediate-signal component of the mass on axial slice 145, producing an initial 182 mL mask.

3. **Verified and corrected** in all three planes:
   - Found the mask leaked superiorly along the femoral vessels (down to the level of axial slice 21) and inferiorly as a thin tail along a draining vessel.
   - A single negative point over-eroded the whole lesion rim, so I undid that and instead used a morphological **opening (4 mm)**, which cleanly stripped both thin vessel protrusions (−6.2 mL) while leaving the tumor surface intact.
   - Checked the boundary against the clean image at multiple axial slices (116, 148, 166, 181) and in coronal/sagittal planes; the outline follows the tumor edge.

4. **Reviewed candidates** — all automatic proposals were surrounding fat, fascia or vessels, so none were accepted.

Final mask: **172.7 mL, single connected component**, saved with medium confidence (residual uncertainty only about the very heterogeneous, less-intense tumor periphery).
